dayTrips.meta_description: Private day tour from Colombo to Sigiriya Lion Rock and Dambulla Cave Temple, both UNESCO sites. Private vehicle, guide and entrance fees included.
dayTrips.overview: Sigiriya is a 5th-century rock fortress rising around 200 metres above the surrounding plain, with royal gardens, the famous Mirror Wall and ancient frescoes near its summit. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Sri Lanka's most recognisable landmarks. Nearby, the Dambulla Royal Cave Temple, also UNESCO-listed, holds a series of Buddhist cave shrines painted and sculpted over more than a thousand years. Both sites sit in the island's Cultural Triangle, roughly 170km from Colombo.

itinerary.text: The climb comes first, while the air is still cool and the stairways are quieter. From the landscaped water gardens you pass the frescoes and the Mirror Wall on your way to the lion’s paws, then take the final stairways to the summit and the ruins of the palace.

dayTrips.bestTime: The Cultural Triangle sits in the dry zone, so this trip runs year-round. January to April and July to August are the driest and clearest. Whatever the month, the climb is far more pleasant started early, which is why the day begins before sunrise.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Colombo to Sigiriya?
faqs.a: About four hours each way for the roughly 170km, using the expressway for the first stretch and the A-road north through Kurunegala after that. That is the reason for the pre-dawn start: it puts you on the rock before the midday heat.

faqs.q: Do I have to climb Sigiriya to enjoy the day?
faqs.a: No. The water gardens, the boulder gardens and the museum at the base are worth the visit on their own, and the view of the rock from Pidurangala nearby is the photograph most people are after. Tell your guide and the day is arranged around what you want to do.

faqs.q: What should I wear?
faqs.a: Shoes you can climb 1,200 steps in, and clothing that covers shoulders and knees for the Dambulla cave temple. Shoes and hats come off at the temple entrance, so socks are worth having on a hot day, because the stone gets warm.

faqs.q: Are the entrance fees included?
faqs.a: Yes. Both the Sigiriya and Dambulla entrance fees are included in the price, along with the vehicle, chauffeur guide, fuel, parking, tolls and lunch.

faqs.q: Can we add Polonnaruwa or a Minneriya safari to the same day?
faqs.a: Honestly, no. Not without making the day unpleasant. Sigiriya and Dambulla already fill it. If you want Polonnaruwa, Minneriya and Kandy as well, the 5-day Cultural Triangle private tour covers all of them at a sane pace.

faqs.q: Can this run as a cruise shore excursion?
faqs.a: Only on a long call. Sigiriya is four hours from Colombo each way, so the ship needs to be in port for the best part of a day. Send us your call and sail-away times and we will tell you honestly whether it fits.

itinerary.text: Pinnawala sits just off the Kandy road, which makes it a natural first stop. The herd is walked down to the Maha Oya river to bathe, and bottle-feeding of the younger animals happens on a fixed schedule, so your guide will time the stop around it.

itinerary.title: Gardens, tea and lunch
itinerary.text: Peradeniya’s Royal Botanical Gardens sit on a loop of the Mahaweli river just outside Kandy: orchid house, palm avenue and a giant Java fig. A working tea factory nearby opens its floors for a walk-through and a tasting, and lunch follows.

itinerary.title: Kandy: the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
itinerary.text: The temple shelters a tooth relic of the Buddha and is the most venerated Buddhist site in the country. Where the schedule allows, your guide will time the visit around one of the daily puja ceremonies, when the drummers play and the inner chamber is opened.

practical.value: Shoulders and knees covered at the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic; shoes are removed at the entrance

practical.label: Pinnawala
practical.value: Feeding and river-bathing run to fixed times, so the stop is planned around them

practical.label: Walking
practical.value: Gentle. The gardens and the temple involve a fair amount of level walking, no climbing

practical.label: Pickup
practical.value: Your Colombo hotel, Bandaranaike Airport or the cruise terminal

dayTrips.bestTime: Kandy sits at about 500m, so it is cooler and greener than the coast all year. December to April is the driest stretch. If you can travel in late July or August, the Esala Perahera (nights of caparisoned tuskers, drummers, dancers and fire) is the single most spectacular thing in the Sri Lankan calendar, and worth planning a trip around.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Colombo to Kandy?
faqs.a: Around three hours each way for the 115km. It is a hill road for the second half, so it is slower than the distance suggests. An early start keeps the day comfortable.

faqs.q: Is Pinnawala included, or is it optional?
faqs.a: It is included in the entrance fees for this day, and it sits directly on the Kandy road, so it costs you no detour. If you would rather skip it and spend longer in Kandy, just say so.

faqs.q: What should I wear for the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic?
faqs.a: Shoulders and knees covered. A shawl or a long skirt over shorts is enough. Shoes and hats come off at the entrance, and white or light clothing is customary though not required.

faqs.q: Can we see the Kandyan dance performance?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The performance runs in the early evening and fits the day if the temple visit goes to plan. It does make for a later return to Colombo, so tell us in advance whether you would like it included.

faqs.q: Can we visit the Esala Perahera on a day trip?
faqs.a: The procession runs on ten nights in late July or August and finishes late, so a same-day return to Colombo makes for a very long night. Most people prefer an overnight in Kandy for it, and we can arrange that, or fold it into a longer private tour.

faqs.q: Is this better as part of a longer tour?
faqs.a: If Kandy is all you want, the day trip does it well. If you also want Sigiriya, Dambulla and Polonnaruwa, the 5-day Cultural Triangle private tour covers the whole region without four hours of driving a day.

dayTrips.name: Galle Day Tour
dayTrips.tags: Galle Fort · UNESCO World Heritage · Southern Coast
dayTrips.seo_title: Galle Day Tour from Colombo | Majesty Tours
dayTrips.meta_description: Private day tour from Colombo to Galle Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site on Sri Lanka's southern coast. Private vehicle, guide and entrance fees included.
dayTrips.overview: Galle Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site built by the Portuguese in the 16th century and heavily fortified by the Dutch in the 17th, its ramparts, lighthouse and colonial streets still intact above the Indian Ocean. It sits roughly 120km south of Colombo along the coastal highway, a journey of under two hours each way.
highlights: The Dutch ramparts and the Galle lighthouse
The colonial streets, galleries and boutiques inside the walls
A Madu River boat safari through the mangroves
Cinnamon Island and a spice garden
The sea turtle hatchery at Kosgoda

itinerary.title: Down the coast to the Madu River
itinerary.text: The southern expressway makes this the easiest of the day trips: Galle is about 120km from Colombo and under two hours away. We break the drive at Balapitiya for a boat safari through the Madu River mangroves.

itinerary.title: The turtle hatchery at Kosgoda
itinerary.text: A short hop south, the hatchery works with eggs recovered from the beaches. There are tanks of hatchlings, a few resident adults that could not be released, and, if the timing lands, a release into the surf.
highlights: Turtle release, when one is scheduled

itinerary.title: Galle Fort
itinerary.text: Portuguese-built in the 16th century, heavily refortified by the Dutch in the 17th, and still lived in: a grid of low colonial houses, churches, galleries and cafés inside a sea wall you can walk the whole way round. Lunch is inside the walls.
highlights: The old town streets and boutiques

itinerary.title: Koggala, Unawatuna and the coast road back
itinerary.text: East of Galle the stilt fishermen perch on their poles in the shallows; west of it, Unawatuna’s sheltered bay and reef are a good swimming stop before turning back north.
highlights: Unawatuna beach and the coral reef
Scenic coastal drive back to Colombo

practical.label: Distance from Colombo
practical.value: About 120km each way, under two hours on the southern expressway

practical.label: Door to door
practical.value: Allow 10–12 hours, depending on how many stops you want

practical.label: Walking
practical.value: Level and easy. The fort is flat, the ramparts are a gentle walk

practical.label: Bring
practical.value: Swimwear and a towel if you want the Unawatuna stop, plus sun protection

practical.label: Best light
practical.value: Sunset from the ramparts is the picture, worth timing the day to end there

practical.label: Pickup
practical.value: Your Colombo hotel, Bandaranaike Airport or the cruise terminal

dayTrips.bestTime: The south coast is at its driest and calmest from December to March, which is also when the sea is best for swimming at Unawatuna. The fort itself is worth walking in any month: the ramparts catch a breeze even in the heat, and a monsoon sky over the lighthouse is no bad thing.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Colombo to Galle?
faqs.a: Under two hours each way on the southern expressway, for about 120km. It is the shortest of our day trips, which is why there is time for the Madu River, the turtle hatchery and the coast as well as the fort itself.

faqs.q: Is the Madu River boat safari included?
faqs.a: The vehicle, chauffeur guide, fuel, parking, tolls, Galle Fort entrance and lunch are included. The boat safari and the hatchery are the standard stops on the way down and we will quote them with the day. Tell us on WhatsApp which of them you want.

faqs.q: Can we swim?
faqs.a: Yes. Unawatuna is the usual stop, a sheltered bay with a reef close in. Bring swimwear and a towel. Between May and September the southwest monsoon can make the sea rough, and your guide will tell you honestly when it is not a swimming day.

faqs.q: Are the stilt fishermen genuine?
faqs.a: The practice is genuine and it is still done, but at the roadside spots near Koggala the men on the poles are largely posing for photographs and will expect a small payment. Your guide will tell you what is reasonable before you get out of the vehicle.

faqs.q: Does this work as a cruise shore excursion from Colombo port?
faqs.a: It is the best of the options for a shorter call: Galle is close enough that even a half-day in port leaves time for the fort. Send us your call and sail-away times and we will build the route to fit them.

faqs.q: Should we stay overnight instead?
faqs.a: Galle Fort after dark, once the day visitors have gone, is a different and better place. If you have the time, the 3-day Southern Coast private tour gives you that plus Mirissa whale watching and the beaches.

dayTrips.name: Yala National Park Safari
dayTrips.tags: Yala National Park · Leopard Safari · Jeep Safari
dayTrips.seo_title: Yala National Park Safari Packages | Majesty Tours
dayTrips.meta_description: Private jeep safari packages at Yala National Park, home to one of the world's highest leopard densities. Vehicle, guide and park fees included.
dayTrips.overview: Yala National Park is famous for having one of the highest leopard densities of any park in the world, alongside elephants, sloth bears and crocodiles. It sits in Sri Lanka's dry southeast, and its main block-one section is typically closed for an annual break in September.
inclusions: Yala National Park Entrance & Jeep Safari Fees
highlights: One of the highest leopard densities of any national park in the world
Wild elephants, sloth bears, spotted deer and crocodiles
A private jeep with a tracker, not a shared seat
Dawn or late-afternoon game drives, when the animals move
Peacocks, painted storks, bee-eaters and the park’s lagoon birdlife
The option of Udawalawe instead, for reliable elephant herds

itinerary.title: Into the park at opening
itinerary.text: Jeeps line up at the gate before it opens. The first hour after sunrise is when leopards are most often on the tracks and the light is at its best, so the early start is not negotiable if you want the sightings.
highlights: The first light along the tank bunds

itinerary.title: The game drive
itinerary.text: Block one of Yala mixes scrub, rock outcrops and lagoons, which is what makes the wildlife so varied. Your tracker works the radio network and the waterholes: leopard, elephant, sloth bear, crocodile, buffalo, spotted deer and a long list of birds.

itinerary.title: Out of the park
itinerary.text: The middle of the day is quiet for game viewing, so the drive ends late morning. Breakfast or lunch is taken outside the park.
highlights: Breakfast or lunch outside the park

itinerary.title: A second drive, if you want one
itinerary.text: The afternoon session runs until the gates close at dusk and is a genuinely different drive, with the animals coming back to the water as the heat drops. Most people who have travelled a long way for a leopard take both sessions.

practical.label: Where it is
practical.value: Sri Lanka’s dry south-east, roughly 300km from Colombo, five to six hours by road

practical.label: Best as
practical.value: An overnight rather than a day return from Colombo: the driving alone is 10–12 hours

practical.label: Game drive times
practical.value: Dawn until mid-morning, and late afternoon until the gates close

practical.label: Annual closure
practical.value: Block one normally closes for its annual break in September

practical.label: The alternative
practical.value: Udawalawe is closer, open all year and far more reliable for large elephant herds

practical.label: Bring
practical.value: Neutral clothing, a hat, sunglasses, a long lens if you have one, and something warm for the dawn start

dayTrips.bestTime: February to July is the driest stretch, when the waterholes shrink and the animals concentrate around them. Those are the best leopard odds of the year. December to March is the most comfortable weather overall. Block one usually closes for its annual break in September; if your dates fall then, Udawalawe or Kumana is the answer and we will say so.

faqs.q: Can I do Yala as a day trip from Colombo?
faqs.a: We would rather you did not. Yala is five to six hours from Colombo each way, so a same-day return means 10–12 hours in a vehicle for one game drive, arriving at the worst time of day for sightings. An overnight nearby costs little more and is a completely different experience.

faqs.q: Am I guaranteed to see a leopard?
faqs.a: No, and anyone who guarantees it is selling something. Yala has one of the highest leopard densities anywhere, which makes the odds good, particularly on a dawn drive in the dry months, but these are wild animals on their own schedule.

faqs.q: Is the jeep private?
faqs.a: Yes. You get your own jeep and tracker rather than a shared seat, which means you decide how long to sit at a sighting and are not moved on for someone else’s schedule.

faqs.q: Udawalawe or Yala: which should we choose?
faqs.a: Udawalawe if you want elephants: the herds there are large, resident and seen on nearly every drive, and it is closer to the coast. Yala if the leopard is what you came for, and you can accept that you might not see one.

faqs.q: Is Yala suitable for children?
faqs.a: Yes, and children generally love it, though the dawn start and several hours of rough track are a lot for very young ones. The afternoon drive is the gentler of the two if you are travelling with small children.

faqs.q: What if Yala is closed for its annual break?
faqs.a: Block one usually closes in September. Other blocks sometimes stay open, and Udawalawe and Kumana run all year. We will tell you what is actually open on your dates rather than sell you a closed park.

experiences.name: Mirissa Whale Watching
experiences.seo_title: Mirissa Whale Watching Tour | Majesty Tours
experiences.meta_description: Private whale watching excursions off Mirissa: blue whales, sperm whales and spinner dolphins. Vehicle, guide and boat excursion fees included.
experiences.overview: Blue whales, sperm whales and spinner dolphins are seen off Mirissa and the East Coast, with the Mirissa season running roughly December to April. This standalone excursion covers the same early-morning boat trip included in our Southern Coast journey, arranged on its own for travellers who only want the whale watching.
highlights: Blue whales, the largest animal that has ever lived
Sperm whales, Bryde’s whales and the occasional whale shark
Spinner dolphins, often in pods of hundreds
An early-morning departure, when the sea is at its flattest
A private transfer to the harbour rather than a shared coach
Season roughly December to April off Mirissa

itinerary.title: The drive to Mirissa harbour
itinerary.text: Boats leave early, because the sea off the south coast is flattest in the first hours of the day and the sightings are better before the wind gets up. We collect you from your hotel in the dark and have you at the harbour for boarding.
highlights: Hotel pickup in a private vehicle
Life jackets and the safety briefing

itinerary.title: Out to the shelf
itinerary.text: The continental shelf drops away close to shore here, which is the whole reason Mirissa works. It is a run of an hour or so out to where the blue whales feed, and the crew and spotters work the horizon for a blow.
highlights: The run out to the feeding grounds
Spinner dolphins, often on the way out

itinerary.title: With the whales
itinerary.text: A blue whale surfaces to breathe several times before the long dive, and the fluke coming up is the moment everyone is waiting for. Boats keep their distance and cut engines. This is watching, not chasing.
highlights: The fluke on a sounding dive

itinerary.title: Back to harbour
itinerary.text: Back alongside by late morning, and back at your hotel with the rest of the day free, or carry on to Galle Fort, Coconut Tree Hill or Unawatuna with your driver.
highlights: Onward to Galle, Unawatuna or your hotel

practical.label: Season
practical.value: Roughly December to April off Mirissa; May to September is the East Coast’s turn, out of Trincomalee

practical.label: Departure
practical.value: Early morning: boats leave the harbour around first light

practical.label: Time at sea
practical.value: Typically three to five hours, depending on how far out the whales are

practical.label: Sea sickness
practical.value: Take a tablet the night before if you are prone to it. The swell is real and the boat sits still while watching

practical.label: Bring
practical.value: Sun protection, a windproof layer, and a camera you do not mind getting sea spray on

practical.label: Included
practical.value: Private vehicle, chauffeur guide, fuel, parking, tolls, boat excursion and park fees, and refreshments

experiences.bestTime: December to April is the Mirissa season, with January to March the most reliable stretch for both blue whales and calm water. Outside those months the southwest monsoon makes the sea off the south coast rough, and the whales have moved round to the east. Between May and September we would send you out of Trincomalee instead.

faqs.q: Am I guaranteed to see a whale?
faqs.a: No. These are wild animals in open ocean and nobody can promise a sighting on any single morning. What Mirissa has is one of the most consistent blue whale seasons in the world, because the continental shelf comes close to shore. In season, the great majority of boats find something.

faqs.q: What is the best month?
faqs.a: January to March. December and April both work, but the sea is flattest and the sightings most reliable in those three months.

faqs.q: How long are we at sea?
faqs.a: Usually three to five hours. If the whales are feeding far out it takes longer, and the crew will keep going rather than turn back early.

faqs.q: Will I get sea sick?
faqs.a: Some people do. The run out is bumpy and the boat then sits more or less still in a swell, which is the part that catches people. If you are prone to it, take a tablet the night before rather than on the morning.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for children?
faqs.a: Yes, with the same caveat about the swell. Younger children usually do better on a calm January morning than at the edges of the season.

faqs.q: Can we combine it with Galle on the same day?
faqs.a: Easily. You are back on land by late morning with your own vehicle and driver waiting, so Galle Fort, Coconut Tree Hill or Unawatuna all fit into the same afternoon.

experiences.bestTime: Cruise calls cluster into the northeast-monsoon months from November to April for the west and south coasts, and May to September for Trincomalee on the east. Because the two coasts run on opposite monsoons, there is no month in which a Sri Lankan port call is a write-off. It only changes which route we would send you on.

faqs.q: Will we get back to the ship on time?
faqs.a: Every route is built backwards from your sail-away time with a margin built in, and we would rather turn down a request than run it too tight. If what you are asking for does not fit your call, we will tell you so before you book.

faqs.q: Where exactly do we meet you?
faqs.a: At the terminal gate, with a name board. Private vehicles are not permitted alongside the berth at Sri Lankan ports, so there is a short shuttle or walk from the gangway to the gate.

faqs.q: Is this cheaper than the ship’s own excursion?
faqs.a: Usually, and it is certainly more private: your own vehicle and guide rather than a shared coach. The trade-off is that an independent excursion is your own arrangement, so we build in more margin than the ship’s operator does.

faqs.q: Can we reach Sigiriya on a port call?
faqs.a: Only on a very long call. Sigiriya is roughly four hours from Colombo each way. If your ship is in for twelve hours or more it works; for anything shorter, Galle or Kandy is the honest answer.

faqs.q: Can you handle a large group?
faqs.a: Yes. The fleet runs from sedans up to 50-seat coaches, so anything from two passengers to a full ship group can be covered. Tell us the numbers and we will size it.

faqs.q: What if the ship arrives late?
faqs.a: We track the arrival and wait. The route is then shortened to whatever the remaining time genuinely allows, and we tell you what has been dropped rather than rushing everything.

Included free with every Majesty Tours journey

itinerary.title: The colonial quarter
itinerary.text: The old commercial heart, where Dutch and British buildings stand in the shadow of the new towers. The 1877 railway station, the Old Parliament facing the sea, and the Dutch Hospital, the oldest building in the city and now a courtyard of restaurants and shops.

itinerary.title: The market streets
itinerary.text: Immediately east of the fort, Pettah is a grid of streets that each sell one thing: a street of hardware, a street of fabric, a street of fruit. The scarlet-and-white Jami-Ul-Alfar mosque rises out of the middle of it.
highlights: The street of a hundred fabric shops
A Hindu kovil in the old town

itinerary.title: Gangaramaya Temple
itinerary.text: Colombo’s best-known temple is a magpie’s nest of a place, with Sri Lankan, Thai, Burmese and Chinese architecture in one compound, with a museum of donated objects and a shrine out on the lake reached by a footbridge.
highlights: The Seema Malaka shrine on the water
Beira Lake and the footbridge at dusk

itinerary.title: Independence Square
itinerary.text: The green, quiet end of the city. The Memorial Hall was built for independence in 1948 in the style of a Kandyan audience hall, and the arcade beneath it is where Colombo comes to walk in the evening.
highlights: The colonnade and the evening walkers

itinerary.title: Galle Face and Port City
itinerary.text: The last stretch runs along the ocean. Galle Face Green fills up at sunset with kite sellers and food carts; beyond it the reclaimed Port City and the Lotus Tower, the tallest structure in South Asia, light up as it gets dark.
highlights: The Lotus Tower, lit up after dark

experiences.bestTime: Colombo works all year. The city is hottest and most humid in March and April, and the late-afternoon run along Galle Face Green is the best of it in any month, which is why the tour is usually timed to end at sunset. October to December brings the heaviest afternoon rain, and an open top deck is less appealing then.

faqs.q: Is the Colombo City Tour really free?
faqs.a: Yes. Book any journey with us and the open-top double-decker sightseeing tour is added at no extra cost. It is not a deposit, an upsell or a timeshare presentation. It is a city tour we include because most travellers pass through Colombo anyway.

faqs.q: When does it happen?
faqs.a: Usually on your first day, as an orientation, or on your last, to fill the hours before a late flight. Both work. Tell us which suits your arrival and departure times.

faqs.q: Can I book it on its own without a tour?
faqs.a: The complimentary version comes with a journey. If you only want the city tour, message us on WhatsApp and we will quote it as a standalone half day with a private vehicle and guide.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: About half a day. That covers the fort, Pettah, Gangaramaya, Independence Square and the seafront at a pace that leaves time to get out and walk.

faqs.q: What should I wear?
faqs.a: Light clothing and sun protection for the open top deck, and something that covers shoulders and knees for Gangaramaya Temple. Shoes come off at the shrine.

faqs.q: Is it worth it if I have been to Colombo before?
faqs.a: If you have only ever passed through the airport, yes. Most people have not actually seen the city. If you know Colombo well, tell us and we will use the time on the coast or in Negombo instead.

experiences.name: Tea Factory Tours & Tastings
experiences.tags: Matale · Kandy · Nuwara Eliya · Guided Cupping Session
experiences.seo_title: Sri Lanka Tea Factory Tours & Tastings | Majesty Tours
experiences.meta_description: Private guided tea factory tours across Sri Lanka's hill country: see the leaf withered, rolled and fired, then compare highland grades in a tasting.
experiences.overview: See the leaf withered, rolled and fired, then compare highland grades in a guided cupping session. Working tea factories across the hill country, around Kandy and Nuwara Eliya, open their floors to private visits, walking you through each stage of processing before a tasting of the estate's own grades.
highlights: A working factory floor, not a museum: withering, rolling, oxidising, firing
A guided cupping session across the estate’s own grades
Meeting the pickers at work in the fields
High-grown Nuwara Eliya against mid-grown Kandy, tasted side by side
The grading room: BOP, BOPF, OP, dust and fannings explained
Factories around Matale, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya

itinerary.title: Where the leaf comes from
itinerary.text: The visit starts in the rows. Two leaves and a bud is the standard pluck, and watching how quickly a practised picker works, and how little of the bush she takes, explains more about tea grades than any display board.
highlights: The baskets weighed in at the end of a round

itinerary.title: The first floor
itinerary.text: Fresh leaf goes into long withering troughs where air is drawn through it for hours to take out the moisture and make it pliable enough to roll. The smell of this floor is the smell of the whole factory.
highlights: Why the leaf has to lose moisture before it can be rolled

itinerary.title: Where black tea becomes black
itinerary.text: Rolling machines bruise and twist the withered leaf to break its cells open, and the oxidation that follows is what turns green leaf coppery brown and builds the flavour. It is timed to the minute and stopped deliberately.
highlights: Oxidation beds and the colour change
How timing decides the character of the tea

itinerary.title: Drying and sorting
itinerary.text: Hot air stops the oxidation dead and dries the tea down for storage. What comes out is then sorted by particle size through a series of meshes, which is all that tea grades really are.
highlights: BOP, BOPF, OP, fannings and dust

itinerary.title: The cupping table
itinerary.text: The point of the visit. Several of the estate’s grades brewed to the same strength and timed the same way, tasted along the table so you can actually tell them apart, and understand what altitude does to a cup.
highlights: How to brew each grade at home

practical.label: Where
practical.value: Working factories around Matale, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya

practical.label: How long
practical.value: Around 45–90 minutes for the factory and tasting, plus the drive and the field walk

practical.label: Fits with
practical.value: A Kandy day trip, the hill country route, or a stop on the way up to Nuwara Eliya

practical.label: Photography
practical.value: Fine on most floors; some factories ask you not to photograph the machinery

practical.label: Closed days
practical.value: Processing usually pauses on Sundays and poya days, so we plan around it

practical.label: Included
practical.value: Private vehicle, chauffeur guide, fuel, parking, tolls and the factory entrance and tasting fees

experiences.bestTime: Any month works for the tour, but the factory is at its most interesting when it is actually running, which means a weekday, and ideally the afternoon or evening, when the day’s plucking is being processed. Processing pauses on Sundays and poya (full moon) days. For the fields themselves, the hill country is clearest from January to April.

faqs.q: Will the factory actually be running?
faqs.a: On a weekday, usually yes, and it is worth planning for. Plucking happens in the morning and processing follows, so an afternoon visit is more likely to catch machinery in motion. Sundays and poya days are generally quiet.

faqs.q: Which factory will we visit?
faqs.a: It depends on where you are and where you are heading. There are working estates around Matale, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya, and we pick one that fits your route rather than detouring you for the sake of a name.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the grades?
faqs.a: Mostly particle size, not quality. After drying, the tea is sorted through meshes: whole-leaf grades like OP at the coarse end, then BOP, BOPF, fannings and dust. Smaller particles brew faster and stronger, which is why they end up in tea bags.

faqs.q: Does altitude really change the taste?
faqs.a: Noticeably, and the tasting is arranged so you can tell. High-grown tea from around Nuwara Eliya is lighter, brisker and more aromatic; mid-grown Kandy tea is fuller and maltier. Side by side at the same brew strength, the difference is obvious.

faqs.q: Can we buy tea at the factory?
faqs.a: Yes, and the estate shop is generally better value and fresher than the airport. Your guide will tell you what is worth buying and what is priced for visitors.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for children?
faqs.a: Yes. The machinery is genuinely interesting to watch and the walk through the fields is easy. The cupping table is the part they will be least patient with, so we keep that end brisk.
